**Initial facts**

- Anne is red.  
- Dave is white.  
- Fiona is not nice.  
- Fiona is quiet.  
- Fiona is young.  
- Gary is quiet.  

**Rule applications**

| # | Rule applied | Premises met | New fact derived | Reason |
|---|--------------|--------------|------------------|--------|
| 4 | Quiet → Red | Fiona is quiet | Fiona is red | Rule 4 |
| 4 | Quiet → Red | Gary is quiet | Gary is red | Rule 4 |
| 2 | Red → Young | Anne is red | Anne is young | Rule 2 |
| 2 | Red → Young | Fiona is red | Fiona is young | Rule 2 (already true) |
| 2 | Red → Young | Gary is red | Gary is young | Rule 2 |
| 6 | Quiet & Young → White | Fiona is quiet & Fiona is young | Fiona is white | Rule 6 |
| 6 | Quiet & Young → White | Gary is quiet & Gary is young | Gary is white | Rule 6 |
| 3 | White → Rough | Dave is white | Dave is rough | Rule 3 |
| 3 | White → Rough | Fiona is white | Fiona is rough | Rule 3 |
| 3 | White → Rough | Gary is white | Gary is rough | Rule 3 |
| 1 | Rough → Not Kind | Dave is rough | Dave is not kind | Rule 1 |
| 1 | Rough → Not Kind | Fiona is rough | Fiona is not kind | Rule 1 |
| 1 | Rough → Not Kind | Gary is rough | Gary is not kind | Rule 1 |

**Conclusion**

We have derived that **Gary is rough**.  
The statement to evaluate is “Gary is not rough.” Since the opposite fact (Gary is rough) has been established, the statement does not follow.

ANSWER: False
